div.head: Ine 53
div.ab: {XCVII} Gif mon forstolenne man befo æt oþrum, ⁊ sie hio hond oðcwolen, sio hine sealde þam men þe hine mon ætbefeng, tieme þonne þone mon to þæs deaden byrgelse, swa oþer fioh swa hit sie, ⁊ cyðe on þam aðe be LX hida, þæt sio deade hond hine sealde. Þonne hæfð he þæt wite afylled mid þy aðe, agife þam agendfrio þone monnan.

If one catches a stolen person [=slave] in another’s possession, and if the man [hand] is dead who sold him to that man in whose possession he was caught, then let [the man who currently has the slave] be vouched to warranty at the dead man’s grave – and likewise for whatever other property it might be – and let him declare with an oath [in the value] of sixty hides, that the dead man [hand] sold it to him. When he has avoided the fine [by means of] the oath, let the owner be given that man.

If a stolen slave is attached [by the law] in the possession of another, and if the man is dead who has sold him to the man in whose possession he is attached, he shall vouch the dead man's grave to warranty for the slave— just as for any other property, whatever it may be — and declare in his oath — [which shall be of the value] of sixty hides — that the dead man sold the slave to him; then he shall have freed himself from the fine by the oath, and he shall give back the slave to [his] owner.

Gif mon forstolenne mon befó æt oðrum, ⁊ sy seo hond oþcwolen, þe hine salde þam men þe hine ætbefeng, tyme ðonne þone man to þære byrgenne ðæs deadan monnes, swa oþer fioh swa hweðer swa hit sy, ⁊ cyðe on þæm aðe be LX hida, þæt sio deade hond hine him sealde; ðonne hæfð he þæt wite afylled mid ðy aðe (⁊) agife ðam agendfrige þone mon.
